==English== {{wp}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|tĕns}}, {{IPA|en|/tɛns/}} * {{audio|en|en-us-tense.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|ɛns|s=1}} * {{homophones|en|tents}} ({{IPAchar|/tɛnts/}}) {{qualifier|in some accents}} * ===Etymology 1=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*tend-|id=stretch}} From {{inh|en|enm|tens}}, from {{der|en|fro|tens}} (modern {{cog|fr|temps}}), from {{der|en|la|tempus}}. {{doublet|en|tempo|tempus}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # {{senseid|en|property indicating a point in time}} {{lb|en|linguistics|uncountable}} The property of indicating the point in time at which an action or state of being occurs or exists. #: {{ux|en|Dyirbal verbs are not inflected for '''tense'''.}} # {{senseid|en|inflected form of a verb}} {{lb|en|linguistics|grammar|countable}} An {{w|inflection|inflected}} form of a verb that indicates {{m|en|tense|id=property indicating a point in time}}. #: {{ux|en|English only has a past '''tense''' and a non-past '''tense'''; it has no future '''tense'''. }} #* {{quote-book|en|url=https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k45595/f201.item|date=18 July 1530|author=[[w:John Palsgrave|Iohan Palſgrave]]|title=Leſclarciſſement de la langue francoyſe{{...}}|publisher=Richard Pynſon, Iohan Haukyns|location=London|oclc=715474564|newversion=reprinted as|year2=1972|publisher2=Slatkine Reprints|location2=Genève|title2=Lesclarcissement de la langue françoyse|chapter=The Introduction|page=32|passage=In ſo moche that if any verbe be of the thyꝛde coniugation
I ſet out all his rotes and '''tenſes'''{{...}}}} # {{senseid|en|grammatical aspect}} {{lb|en|grammar|countable|proscribed}} A grammatical {{m|en|aspect|id=grammatical quality of a verb}}. # {{senseid|en|grammar}} {{lb|en|grammar|countable|proscribed}} A verb form or construction indicating a combination of {{m|en|tense|id=property indicating a point in time}}, {{m|en|aspect|id=grammatical quality of a verb}}, and {{m|en|mood|id=grammatical}}. #: {{ux|en|The "simple present" '''tense''' in English can have several meanings.}} #:: Habits: I '''walk''' my dog every day. #:: Stative verbs: You '''are''' happy. #:: Facts: The Earth '''revolves''' around the Sun. #:: Etc. #: {{ux|en|The Spanish teacher told the student to use the imperfect '''tense''' instead of the preterite '''tense'''.}} =====Usage notes===== * Some English-language authorities only consider inflected forms of verbs (i.e. the present and past tenses) as tenses, and not periphrastic forms such as the simple future with {{m|en|will}}. * Grammatically tense (the location of an event in time: past, present, future) is often distinguished from {{m|en|aspect|id=grammatical quality of a verb}} (how an event occurs or is viewed by the speaker: finished, ongoing, habitual, etc.). So ''I am eating'' and ''I was eating'' have different tenses (present and past) but the same aspect (continuous), whereas ''I was eating'' and ''I had eaten'' have the same tense (past) and different aspects (continuous and perfect). However, it is common in English (especially in language teaching) to refer to aspects as tenses (e.g. ''the perfect tense'', ''the continuous tense''). =====Derived terms===== {{col|en|absolute tense|aorist tense|tense harmony|conditional tense|continuous tense|future tense|hodiernal tense|imperfect tense|past historic tense|past imperfect tense|past tense|perfect tense|pluperfect tense|present tense|preterite tense|primary tense|progressive tense|relative tense|secondary tense|simple tense|supine tense|tensal|compound tense|tenseless}} =====Related terms===== * ''See:'' [[:Category:en:Tenses]] =====Translations===== {{trans-top|verb forms distinguishing time}} * Afrikaans: * Albanian: * Arabic: * Armenian: * Azerbaijani: * Belarusian: * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Chinese: * Chuvash: * Czech: * Danish: * Dutch: * Estonian: * Faroese: * Finnish: * French: * Georgian: * German: * Greek: * Hebrew: * Hindi: * Hungarian: * Icelandic: * Irish: * Isoko: * Italian: * Japanese: * Kazakh: * Korean: * Kyrgyz: * Latin: * Latvian: * Lithuanian: * Macedonian: * Malayalam: * Māori: * Middle English: * Norman: * Norwegian: * Persian: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|вре́мя|n}} * Serbo-Croatian: * Slovak: * Slovene: * Spanish: * Swahili: * Swedish: * Tagalog: * Tajik: * Tamil: * Telugu: * Thai: * Tibetan: * Turkish: * Udmurt: * Ukrainian: * Uyghur: * Uzbek: * Vietnamese: * Welsh: {{trans-bottom}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|grammar|transitive}} To apply a tense to. #: {{co|en|'''tensing''' a verb}} ===Etymology 2=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*tend-|id=stretch}} Borrowed from {{bor|en|la|tēnsus}}, one form of the past participle of {{m|la|tendō|t=stretch}}. ====Adjective==== {{en-adj|er}} # [[show|Showing]] [[sign]]s of [[stress]] or [[strain]]; not [[relax]]ed. #: {{syn|en|stressed|unrelaxed|taut}} #: {{ux|en|You need to relax, all this overtime and stress is making you '''tense'''.}} #* {{quote-book|en|date=2009-10-21|author=Richard Steinberg|title=The 4 Phase Man: A Novel|publisher=Bantam|isbn=9780307571830 |text="Attention," the '''tense''' man called out in Greek. "Actually[,] I have sent them away. I thought that only the two of us should share the special surprise." He gave a '''tense''' smile.}} # Characterized by [[strain]] (on the nerves, emotions, etc). {{q|Compare {{m|en|charged}}.}} #* {{quote-book|en|date=2022-06-16|author=Marc B. DeGeorge|title=A Call to the Sky|publisher=MuseMarc Studio LLC|isbn=9781956487107 |text=Chi stops, but her eyes continue to pierce right through me and into Karima. A '''tense''' moment later, she drops her eyes back to the terminal and scans the data once more. The showdown is over, at least for the moment.}} # Pulled [[taut]], without any [[slack]]. # {{lb|en|phonetics|of a vowel}} Produced with relative constriction of the [[vocal tract]]. #: {{antonym|en|lax}} =====Derived terms===== {{col|en|hypertense|overtense|tensely|tensen|tenseness|tensible|tensification|tensor|ultratense|untense |tense vowel}} =====Related terms===== * {{l|en|tend}} * {{l|en|tension}} * {{l|en|tent}} * {{l|en|intense}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|showing stress or strain}} * Afrikaans: * Arabic: * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Chinese: * Czech: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Estonian: * Finnish: * French: * German: * Greek: * Hebrew: * Hungarian: * Icelandic: * Japanese: * Macedonian: * Māori: * Plautdietsch: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|напряжённый}} * Spanish: * Swedish: * Turkish: * Ukrainian: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|pulled taut}} * Bulgarian: * Estonian: * Finnish: * German: * Greek: * Portuguese: * Russian: {{t+|ru|туго́й}}, {{t+|ru|натя́нутый}} * Spanish: * Swedish: * Turkish: * Ukrainian: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|produced with relative constriction of the vocal tract}} * Russian: {{t+|ru|напряжённый}} {{trans-bottom}} {{checktrans-top}} * Georgian: {{t-check|ka|დაძაბული}} {{trans-bottom}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{senseid|en|make tense}}{{lb|en|transitive}} To [[make]] tense. # {{senseid|en|become tense}}{{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[become]] tense. =====Derived terms===== {{col|en|tense up|overtense|untense}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top-see|make tense|tension}} * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Czech: * Dutch: * Estonian: * Finnish: * French: * German: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Spanish: * Ukrainian: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|become tense}} * Bulgarian: * Finnish: * French: * German: * Polish: * Spanish: * Ukrainian: {{trans-bottom}} ===Anagrams=== * {{anagrams|en|a=eenst|ESnet|Enets|NEETs|Stene|Tenes|enset|neets|seent|senet|sente|steen|teens}}
